title: Namchi and Ravangla on a budget
meta_description: What Namchi and Ravangla really cost in 2026: shared jeep fares, budget rooms, homestays, entry fees and a 3-night plan from about ₹7,500 per person.
summary: Namchi and Ravangla are the cheapest comfortable corner of Sikkim. Shared jeeps from Siliguri cost about ₹250–450 a seat, clean rooms run ₹1,200–2,500, there are no permits for Indians, and a careful couple can do three nights from NJP for roughly ₹7,500–9,000 each, food and sightseeing included.

sections.heading: Why the south is the budget end of Sikkim
paras: South Sikkim, now officially Namchi district, sits low and close to the plains. Namchi town is at about 1,315 m and Ravangla at about 2,100 m, so nights are cool rather than freezing, and you do not pay for the heavy-duty vehicles, permits and minimum stays that push up the cost of North Sikkim. Indian travellers need no protected-area permit anywhere on the usual Namchi–Ravangla circuit. The only state charge is the ₹50 per tourist Tourism Sustainable Development fee that hotels collect at check-in, valid for 30 days, with under-5s exempt. Check current status before you travel.

Distances are short too. Namchi is about 100 km from Siliguri via Melli, a 3.5 to 4 hour drive, and Ravangla is another 26 km and roughly an hour up the hill. That means one day of travel in, one day out, and every sight in between within an hour of your bed. Short drives are the single biggest saving in a mountain trip, because in Sikkim you pay for the car by the day, not by the kilometre.

sections.heading: Getting there on shared jeeps
paras: Shared jeeps (Bolero, Sumo and similar, ten seats or so) are how most people in Sikkim travel, and they are the core of a budget trip. From Siliguri, jeeps for Namchi, Jorethang and Ravangla leave from the Sikkim jeep stands near the SNT bus terminus, mostly in the morning. Go early: after about 1 pm the choice thins out. From NJP station take an auto or a local cab to Siliguri first, or look for a direct jeep at the station stand in season.

From Gangtok, jeeps for Namchi and Ravangla run from the Vajra taxi stand, which handles the west and south. Inside the district, Namchi to Ravangla and Namchi to Jorethang jeeps run through the day. If the four front-and-middle seats matter to you, pay for two seats and say so at the counter; it is normal and saves a cramped back row on the hairpins.

One road warning that affects your budget: the main Siliguri road runs up the Teesta along NH10 as far as Melli, and NH10 closes in the monsoon after landslides. The fallback is via Kalimpong or Algarah, which adds time and sometimes a night. Check current status before you travel, and keep a spare half day in a June–September plan.

sections.heading: Where to sleep for less
paras: Namchi has the wider choice of cheap rooms because it is a district headquarters with a steady flow of officials, traders and pilgrims. Plain, clean doubles with hot water start at about ₹1,200–1,500 a night off season and ₹1,800–2,500 in October and May. The pilgrim lodge at Char Dham on Solophok hill offers simple rooms at modest rates and is popular with families doing the temple complex at dawn; book ahead around festivals.

Ravangla is smaller and a notch more expensive in peak weeks, because most rooms face the Kangchenjunga range and the town fills with weekend visitors from Gangtok and Siliguri. Budget rooms run about ₹1,500–2,500. For the best value of all, sleep in a homestay at Kewzing or Yangang, a short drive from Ravangla: about ₹1,200–2,000 per person a night with dinner and breakfast, home-grown vegetables and a family who will tell you where the path to the monastery starts.

Two money rules for rooms: ask for the room rate before you see the room, because walk-in prices drop sharply between November and February and in the monsoon; and ask whether the ₹50 entry fee and any service charge are already in the quote.

sections.heading: Food, entry fees and small costs
paras: Eating cheaply here is easy. A vegetarian or chicken thali in a Namchi or Ravangla dhaba costs about ₹120–220, a plate of momos ₹60–100, a bowl of thukpa ₹80–120, and milk tea ₹15–25. Buy fruit and snacks at the Namchi market rather than at viewpoints. Packaged water is sold everywhere, but carry a refillable bottle; most hotels will fill it.

Entry fees at the main sights are small and change from time to time, so treat these as indicative. Char Dham has charged about ₹50 per person; the Guru Padmasambhava statue at Samdruptse a token fee; Buddha Park at Ravangla about ₹50 for Indians and ₹100 for foreign nationals; the Temi Tea Garden is free to walk, with tea and packets to buy at the estate outlet. Monasteries such as Ralang and Ngadak do not charge, though a small offering is welcome.

sections.heading: Sightseeing without overspending
paras: The trick in Namchi is to hire a small car for a half day rather than a full day. The Char Dham complex, the Samdruptse statue, Namchi Rock Garden and the old Ngadak monastery are all within 10 km of the town centre, and a reserved Alto or WagonR class car will usually do them in four to five hours for about ₹1,500–2,000. Split between four people, that is less than a shared jeep from Siliguri.

In Ravangla, Buddha Park is about 1 km from the market and walkable. Ralang Monastery is about 6 km away and the Temi Tea Garden about 20 km, so a single reserved car (about ₹2,000–2,800 for the day) covers both, with Borong or Kewzing added if you start early. Tendong Hill costs nothing but stamina: the forest path from Damthang to the 2,600 m summit takes 2.5 to 3 hours up.

sections.heading: A three-night plan and what it costs
paras: Here is a real budget for two people sharing, travelling by shared jeep, sleeping in budget rooms and splitting one half-day car in Namchi and one full-day car in Ravangla. It assumes October or March prices, and it is indicative: fares and room rates move with the season and fuel prices, so check current status before you travel.

Day 1, jeep from Siliguri to Namchi, evening at Char Dham. Day 2, morning Samdruptse and Rock Garden, afternoon jeep to Ravangla. Day 3, Buddha Park at opening time, then Ralang and Temi by car. Day 4, early jeep back to Siliguri for an afternoon train or flight. Per person, it comes to roughly ₹7,500–9,000.

sections.heading: When a package beats doing it yourself
paras: Doing it yourself is cheapest for a couple or a group of friends with flexible days. A package starts to make sense when you are four or more with luggage, travelling with parents or small children, or arriving on a late flight into Bagdogra, when shared jeeps have stopped for the day. A private small car for three or four days, with one driver who knows where to wait at Char Dham and which road is shut, often costs only ₹1,500–2,500 per person more than jeeps for a family of four. Our budget South Sikkim trips are built on exactly that arithmetic, and we show the breakdown on every package.

faqs.q: How much does a 3-day Namchi and Ravangla trip cost on a budget?
faqs.a: Roughly ₹7,500–9,000 per person for three nights from Siliguri if two people share budget rooms, use shared jeeps and split a car for local sightseeing. A private small car for the whole trip adds about ₹2,000–3,500 per person for a couple, less for four. These are indicative 2026 figures; check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Do Indian tourists need a permit for Namchi or Ravangla?
faqs.a: No. Indian nationals need no protected-area permit for Namchi, Ravangla, Temi, Borong or the usual South Sikkim sights. Hotels collect the ₹50 per person Tourism Sustainable Development fee at check-in, valid 30 days. Foreign nationals need the Restricted Area Permit to enter Sikkim, applied for online via e-FRRO. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Where do shared jeeps to Namchi leave from in Siliguri?
faqs.a: From the Sikkim jeep stands near the SNT bus terminus in Siliguri, mostly in the morning. Jeeps for Namchi, Jorethang and Ravangla leave when full; after about 1 pm the choice drops. From NJP station, take an auto or local cab to Siliguri first. A seat to Namchi costs roughly ₹250–350.

Yes, for most things. Budget rooms in Namchi start around ₹1,200–1,500 against ₹1,800–2,500 in central Gangtok, local cars cost less because the sights are close together, and food prices are lower outside the MG Marg area. Gangtok has more choice at every level, but Namchi gives more room for your rupee.

faqs.q: What is the cheapest way to see Char Dham and Samdruptse?
faqs.a: Share a reserved small car for a half day from Namchi town, about ₹1,500–2,000 for the car. Char Dham, Samdruptse, Rock Garden and Ngadak monastery are all within 10 km. Local shared taxis also run past Char Dham, and fit walkers can walk down from Samdruptse, but the car saves a lot of time for little money.

faqs.q: How much is a homestay near Ravangla?
faqs.a: Homestays at Kewzing and Yangang usually charge about ₹1,200–2,000 per person a night including dinner and breakfast, with home-cooked food. Rates rise a little in October and May and around long weekends. Book a day or two ahead in season; off season you can usually find a room the same day.

faqs.q: Can I do Namchi and Ravangla in a weekend from Siliguri?
faqs.a: Yes, two nights is enough for the main sights if you leave Siliguri by 8 am. Do Char Dham and Samdruptse on day one, Ravangla and Buddha Park on day two, and drive back on day three. It is rushed for Temi or Tendong; add a night for either.

faqs.q: What does food cost in Namchi and Ravangla?
faqs.a: A thali costs about ₹120–220, momos ₹60–100 a plate, thukpa ₹80–120, tea ₹15–25. Hotel restaurants charge more, about ₹300–500 for a meal. Most budget travellers spend ₹500–700 a day each on food. Homestays include dinner and breakfast in their rate.

faqs.q: Is the road from Siliguri to Namchi open in the monsoon?
faqs.a: Usually, but not always. The route uses NH10 up the Teesta to Melli, and NH10 closes after landslides in heavy rain. The alternatives are via Kalimpong or Algarah, which add time. Keep a buffer day between June and September and check current status before you travel.
